Options.OPTION[CDLC.BusDriver.CDLC.BusDr: Drive your city's bus lines with CSL Driving Life Core. Open the bus panel (Alt+B by default), pick a line, take a bus from the depot or over from service, and serve the stops: stop inside the painted boarding zone and press F to open the doors. Passengers board and alight by themselves and pay the line's fare into the city budget.
Options.OPTION_DESCRIPTION[CDLC.BusDrive: Paint the boarding zone at the stops of the line you drive (only during a shift).
Show the zones of all stops of the line, not only the next one.
Draw the line's path to the next stop as a dashed line on the road.
Show the next stop, distance, passengers and the door state at the top of the screen.

No guide line and no other stops' zones on the road: only the next stop's boarding zone shows, fainter. The shift still follows the route and the stops (the panel at the top, the prompts and the announcements stay). Switch it with the immersive key (I) while driving.
During a shift: hide or show the guide line and the stop zones on the road (the next stop's zone stays, fainter).
Open or close the bus panel.
At a stop: tap to open or close the doors, hold to close them at once. Only active during a shift.

Switches the left indicator on; the same key again switches it off, the right key switches over. It cancels by itself when the wheel comes back after a turn, like a real indicator stalk. Works while you drive a bus, no shift needed; the bus never indicates on its own.

Switches the right indicator on; the same key again switches it off, the left key switches over. It cancels by itself when the wheel comes back after a turn. Works while you drive a bus, no shift needed.
Restore the default keys.
The pad rumbles with the engine and the road, a gear shift, hard braking and the doors. Only while you drive the bus.
How strong the rumble is.

PS5 pad only: the brake trigger (L2) gets stiffer with the brake, the throttle trigger (R2) pushes back and buzzes through a gear shift. Needs the pad to reach the game directly: turn Steam Input off for this game. With CSL Driving Life Core's pad driving the triggers are the pedals, so the stiffness follows your own foot.

PS5 pad over USB only: the throttle trigger (R2) shivers with the engine, faster with the revs and stronger with the pedal; the brake trigger (L2) pulses under hard braking; both give a jolt over a bump, and R2 buzzes through a gear shift. Works with or without 'DualSense triggers' (which adds the stiffness). Needs the pad to reach the game directly: turn Steam Input off for this game. Follows 'Rumble strength'.

Open or close the bus panel from the pad. By default a combination: hold the right stick (R3) and press X / square. The pad's buttons are read from the pad itself, so they work whatever the game thinks you are using.
At a stop: tap to open or close the doors, hold to close them at once. Only active during a shift.
Left indicator on or off. Works while you drive a bus.
Right indicator on or off. Works while you drive a bus.
Hide or show the guide line and the stop zones. Only active during a shift.

Options.OPTION_DESCRIPTION[CDLC.BusDrive: In the driver's view (first person) of a bus, draw the inside of the bus around you: the driver's cab with the steering wheel and dials, the doors, seats, poles and lights. Built to the size of the bus you drive.
Options.OPTION[CDLC.BusDriver.CDLC.BusDr: Start shifts in the driver's view
Options.OPTION_DESCRIPTION[CDLC.BusDrive: Switch to the driver's view when a shift starts. The camera view key (C) switches between the driver's view and the chase view at any time.

Moves the camera of the driver view up or down from the seat the bus model gives it, in centimetres (up to 25 either way; up is positive). For a taller or a shorter driver. It applies at once, in the driver view of a shift and of a ride; the mirrors show what they would for the moved eye.
Options.OPTION[CDLC.BusDriver.CDLC.BusDr: Driver view: eye left and right
Options.OPTION_DESCRIPTION[CDLC.BusDrive: Moves the camera of the driver view to the left or right of the seat the bus model gives it, in centimetres (up to 25 either way; right is positive, on whichever side the driver sits). It applies at once, in the driver view of a shift and of a ride; the mirrors show what they would for the moved eye.
Options.OPTION[CDLC.BusDriver.CDLC.BusDr: Start the shift when you take a bus of a line
Options.OPTION_DESCRIPTION[CDLC.BusDrive: Taking a bus that is running on a passenger line directly (the driving mod's key, or Drive in its info panel) starts the shift on that line with this bus, as Take over in the bus panel does: the stops, the doors, the passengers and the guidance. A bus on no line (parked, in its depot) is driven freely as before. Off: only the bus panel starts a shift.

Draw the whole bus you drive, outside included, instead of the game's bus: a modern low-floor bus in the line's colours with clear windows (the lit saloon is seen from outside), LED destination signs on the front, the side and the rear, turning wheels, head lamps (dipped and high beam, lighting the road), tail, brake and reversing lamps, and the indicators and hazard lamps you switch on with the keys. Needs CSL Driving Life Core 0.10. Only for our own buses: the mod's CDLC City Bus 12 m and the buses of the CDLC vehicle packs (each its own asset mod, e.g. CDLC.Bus.SWB6710EV01G). Official, DLC and workshop buses keep their own body outside; the cab inside is still drawn. A workshop bus with a CDLC sign overlay (a <prefab>.cdlb-signs.json beside its .cok) keeps its body and wears our LED signs.

In the driver's view the exterior mirrors show what is behind and beside the bus: a small camera in each mirror (a low resolution image, the mirrors updated in turn, one a frame at most; shadows and screen effects left out). It costs some frame time; if the game slows down, lower Mirror quality first, then turn this off. The game only prepares what is around the main view, so traffic right behind the bus may not show in them.

How much the glass of our buses computes (the driven bus, the AI buses of the vehicle packs and the stations' glass). High: as it always was. Balanced: the glass writes no motion vectors of its own, so the picture behind it stays sharp while moving with anti-aliasing or an upscaler, and no depth offset (cheaper). Fast: also no fog on the glass, and the glass of the bus you sit in is not drawn in the views from a seat (open windows: sharp, and the least work for the graphics card). Needs CDL Assets 0.6.2 for the glass itself.

How often the real mirrors are redrawn and how much detail they show. High: each mirror 20 times a second on its own (the sharpest, the most frame time). Medium (default): 30 images a second shared by the mirrors in view (about 10 each with three), minor screen effects left out. Low: 15 a second shared (about 5 each), half the resolution, no road markings, glow or refraction in the mirrors (the least frame time). Only mirrors you can see are redrawn, and none outside the cab view. Applies at once.

A line named with a prefix before its number (K3, BRT1, N12, 夜12路: name the line so in the game) shows the prefix in its own colour on the bus's LED signs, on the next-stop screen and in the panel. Pairs of prefix = colour, separated by ";": colour names (red, green, blue, cyan, yellow, amber, orange, white, purple, magenta, pink; 红 绿 蓝 青 黄 橙 白 紫) or #RRGGBB; "*" for any other prefix. Default: K=green; BRT=green; B=green; N=blue; 夜=blue; 快=red; Y=cyan; 游=cyan; *=red.

A wrap on the bus you drive: pictures for its sides, front, rear and roof (an itasha, an advertising livery, your city's design), with see-through (PNG alpha) parts; on models whose wrap covers the windows and doors the picture goes onto them too, doors included, and see-through edges get a white outline. Wraps are zip files per vehicle model (a wrap never works on another model). Manage them in the Bus Driver panel, tab Wraps: new wrap from the model's template, load, unload, open the folder. The wrap reloads a few seconds after its zip changes. Only the bus you drive, seen from outside.

Opens ModsData/CDLC.BusDriver/Wraps (with a README) in Explorer. After you have driven a bus it also holds "template", the layout of that bus's sides to paint over. New folders show in the list after you press this.
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Readme:
CSL Driving Life : Bus Driver - body wraps

A wrap is a zip: Wraps/<vehicle model>/<name>.zip. Every model has its own folder; a wrap made for one model is never
offered or used on another (its pictures are drawn to that model's faces). Inside the zip:
  left.png   the left side as you look at it: the front of the bus at the picture's LEFT edge
  right.png  the right side as you look at it: the front at the picture's RIGHT edge (a side without its picture takes the other's)
  front.png  the lower front as you look at it, round its corners: the bus's right corner at the picture's left
  rear.png   the rear below and beside the rear window as you look at it
  roof.png   the roof from above, from one roof edge over to the other: the front at the picture's LEFT edge, the
             bus's left side at the BOTTOM (it continues left.png's top edge)
  wrap.json  the model and the layout version the pictures were drawn for (copied from the template)
  thumb.png  optional: the picture shown in the manager
Pictures are PNGs with a transparent channel: a pixel's alpha is its opacity (the paint, window or door shows through the
transparent parts, a soft edge stays soft). On models whose wrap covers the windows and doors, the edge of a see-through part
(alpha under half) in a window or door gets a
white outline automatically (its width is outlineMm in wrap.json). Doors carry their part of the picture when they open.
Start from the model's template.zip (empty pictures, guide/*.png maps of what each area is, README, the model's numbers):
in the game, Bus Driver panel > Wraps > New wrap makes wrap-N.zip from it; unpack it, paint, zip the files again (the
pictures at the top level of the zip). The wrap reloads a couple of seconds after the zip changes. Only the bus you drive
shows the wrap, seen from outside.
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.Title: Bus Driver wrap template for {0} (layout {1})
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.Intro:
Paint on left.png, right.png, front.png, rear.png and roof.png (empty = transparent), at any size in the same proportions
(wrap.json: "info" gives each face's size in metres and the suggested pixels). guide/<face>.png is the model seen from outside
straight on (the same projection the pictures are mapped with) and shows what each area is:
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.Paint: light grey   body paint: the picture shows; where you leave it transparent the bus's own paint shows (its line colour, or the model's fixed colours)
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.PaintWindow: (on this model the window frames, the pillars between the windows and the black band above them are body paint too)
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.Glass: blue stripes  window glass: the picture covers it; transparent = see-through, and the edge of a see-through part gets a white outline
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.Door: green         door leaves: the picture goes with the door when it opens (transparent = see-through, with the white outline)
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.Pillar: {0} outline  pillar {1}: body paint, the picture covers it
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.Joint:
pink dashes  a joint: the sides and the roof are one picture over the {0} sections (from the front {1} m); the bellows between them takes no picture,
               so what crosses the line is parted there by the bellows
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.Trim: mid grey     lamps, plates, grilles, window bars and trim stand in front of the picture
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.Hidden: dark grey    part of the bus the picture does not cover: {0}wheel arches, lamps, and the surface that turns towards the neighbouring picture
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.HiddenFront: the windscreen and its frame (but for the outlined pillars),
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.Outside: black-blue   outside the bus (the silhouette seen from this side)
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.Grid: a line every metre; the front edge of the sides and the roof is red
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.Rule:
Rule: a pixel's alpha is its opacity (alpha under half in a window or door also counts as see-through for the white outline). Zip the pictures (and wrap.json) at the top level of a zip named after your wrap
and put it in this folder. It is only used on {0}.
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.InfoAlpha: the picture's alpha is its opacity (alpha blended: the body, window or door shows through transparent parts, a soft edge stays soft)
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Template.InfoOutline: in the window and door areas the edge of a see-through part (alpha under 0.5) gets a white outline of outlineMm
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Err.OtherModel: it was made for {0}, not {1} (wraps of different models do not mix)
CDLC.BusDriver.Wrap.Err.OtherLayout: it was made for layout {0} of {1}, which is now layout {2}: use the new template
Options.OPTION_DESCRIPTION[CDLC.BusDrive: Show the game's passengers on board as people in the bus, seated and standing: the bus looks as full as the game's load (passengers over capacity) on its seats and standing places, the seats taken first and a few standing by the doors. They board and leave one by one at the stops. The driver sits at the wheel when the bus is seen from outside.

The passengers and the driver are the game's own citizens: each passenger looks as the game made that resident (clothes, hair, face), seated, standing, holding a strap; the driver at the wheel. Off: simple figures, which cost less frame time in a full bus.
While the doors are open the bus lowers its door side on the air springs (with the hiss of the air) and rises again when they close. Needs CSL Driving Life Core 0.10.
Assets.DESCRIPTION[CDLCBus12]: A modern 12 m low-floor city bus with three doors, clear windows and LED destination signs, in the line's colour. From CSL Driving Life : Bus Driver.

CDLC.BusDriver.UI.WrapHint: New wrap copies this model's template.zip (empty pictures to paint on, guide pictures marking body, windows, doors and parts in front, the model's numbers) as wrap-N.zip and opens the folder: unpack it, paint left, right, front, rear and roof.png (transparent shows what is under it; in windows and doors the edge of a see-through part gets a white outline), zip the pictures again at the top level. The bus changes a few seconds after the zip is saved. Only the bus you drive, seen from outside.

Options.OPTION_DESCRIPTION[CDLC.BusDrive: A chime before each announcement. Pulling away: "The bus is moving off, please hold on. Route 3 to X. The next stop is Y." 150 m before the stop: "Approaching Y. Please get ready to leave by the rear door." (or that the bus will not stop there, when no one gets on or off). Doors open: "This is Y. Please mind your step." The final stop has its own announcements. They also play while you ride a bus as a passenger (without the "not stopping" one: the game does not tell which stops a bus passes). The voice is made in the background and kept on disk; the game never waits for it.

Automatic: the best one available (Azure with a key, else Piper when installed, else the Windows voice). Piper: the open-source offline engine with its Chinese (huayan) and English (lessac) voices, installed with the button below. Microsoft neural: Xiaoxiao (Chinese) or Jenny (English) from the Azure Speech service with your own key. Windows: the voices installed on this PC (Huihui, Zira). Chime only: no voice, the screen shows the text.
Loudness of the chime and the voice (within the game's sound effects volume).
Say the route and its destination when pulling away: "Route 3 to X."
The spoken sentences are kept in %LOCALAPPDATA%\CDLC\tts (about 50 KB each). When the folder grows past this size the oldest files are removed.
Deletes every spoken sentence kept on disk. They are made again when needed.

Options.OPTION_DESCRIPTION[CDLC.BusDrive: Key 1 of your Azure "Speech" resource (portal.azure.com, Keys and Endpoint). Stored in this mod's settings file only and sent to Microsoft's service only.
The resource's region as in its endpoint: eastasia, southeastasia, japaneast, westeurope, eastus, ...
HTTP proxy for the service, as host:port (for example 127.0.0.1:7897). Empty: the system's proxy. "none": a direct connection.

Downloads Piper (MIT licence, rhasspy/piper, 22 MB) and its voices for the game's language and English (63 MB each). The voices have their own licences and you download them for your own use: English lessac is trained on a research-only dataset (Blizzard 2013) and the other voices are fine-tuned from it, and the datasets of the Chinese voice huayan and the Russian voice irina have no stated licence into %LOCALAPPDATA%\CDLC\piper, in the background through the proxy below or the system's. A notice appears when it is done; from then on the announcements use it.
CDLC.BusDriver.Piper.Title: CSL Driving Life : Bus Driver
CDLC.BusDriver.Piper.Installing: Downloading the open-source voice (Piper, about 150 MB) in the background. A notice follows when it is done.
CDLC.BusDriver.Piper.Done: The open-source voice (Piper) is installed; the announcements use it from now on.
CDLC.BusDriver.Piper.Failed: The open-source voice (Piper) could not be installed; see the log (CDLC.BusDriver.Mod.log). Check the proxy setting.
CDLC.BusDriver.Hint.Hazard: Hazard warning lamps (or both indicator buttons together)
Options.OPTION_DESCRIPTION[CDLC.BusDrive: Where the head lamp switch is each time you take a bus. The light key steps it: automatic (dipped beam when it gets dark), low beam, high beam, off (only the daytime running strip). Works on our own buses; the game's other buses keep their own lights.

The head lamps of our own buses also shine on the road (two spot lights per bus, no shadows): the dipped beam wide and short, the high beam narrow and far. Off: the lamps only glow. Switched off by daylight.
How bright the spot lights on the road are, 100 % being the mod's setting. Turn it down if the road looks bleached at night, up if the beams hardly show.

The buses of the vehicle packs, the mod's own bus and buses by other authors with a CDLC sign overlay (a <prefab>.cdlb-signs.json beside their .cok) show their line and terminus on their LED signs (front, door side, rear) also when the game drives them; "Not in service" when they are off a line. Switch it off to save the work.
How far from the camera the AI buses' signs light up, in metres. Shorter costs less; beyond about 100 m the text cannot be read anyway.

The LED screens of station packs (a bus station asset made for this mod, such as the CDL bus interchange) show live departures: each bay's lines with their terminus and the nearest bus (at the stop, arriving, or how many stops away), and the people waiting. The game gives no arrival times, so the boards count stops. Switch it off to save the work; the screens then stay dark.

The outside LED signs of our buses, the one you drive and the AI buses. Shanghai (default): 32 rows of dots, twice as fine as before, the route number as tall as the sign, then › and the stop: in Chinese with its English line under it (as Shanghai's bus signs; the English made from the stop name's pinyin), a long name scrolling; the route prefix keeps its own colour (option "Route prefix colours"). Classic: the 16-row signs of earlier versions. Buses with printed boards keep them.

With the Shanghai style, the rear sign shows "Braking" (刹车注意) while the bus brakes on the move and a moment after, and "Turning left / right" (车辆左转 / 车辆右转) with an arrow while it indicates; an AI bus follows the game's own braking and turning. Off: the rear sign shows the route only.
Both indicators flash together until you press the key again. While you drive a bus; no shift is needed. Pressing both indicator keys together does the same.
Steps the head lamp switch: automatic, low beam, high beam, off. While you drive one of our buses; no shift is needed.
The high beam for as long as the key is held, whatever the switch says; the switch comes back when you let go.
The hazard lamps from the pad. By default R3 + D-pad right; pressing both indicator buttons (LB and RB) together switches them as well.
Steps the head lamp switch: automatic, low beam, high beam, off.
The high beam for as long as the button is held.
